text:
Caroline S: :rotating_light: CS-4321 reporting repeated 504s hitting /v1/generate for hosted inference. Customer says errors spike during hour-long bursts and their requests time out after ~30s. They reported it started after a weekend traffic surge.

Alex C: Thanks, Caroline. Any correlating alarms?

Support Bot: Alert: gateway-504-rate increased in prod-us-east-1 - 2024-11-09T03:12:05Z (count: 87 in 5m). Associated upstream: model-pool-a.

Sarah L: I can confirm downstream traces show requests queued >10s then gateway returns 504. KEDA scaled events show rapid scaleDown then delayed scaleUp.

Mike R: Noted. Can someone paste the HPA and ScaledObject config? We suspect HPA target CPU vs KEDA poll/activation mismatch.

Julia P: Paste from prod: 
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-pool-a-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
---
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-pool-a-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: model-pool-a-deployment
  pollingInterval: 30 # seconds
  cooldownPeriod: 300 # seconds
  triggers:
  - type: queue
    metadata:
      queueLength: "50"
```

Caroline S: Also noticed readinessProbe has a long timeout: initialDelaySeconds: 10, periodSeconds: 10, timeoutSeconds: 5. Pod logs show model init ~18-25s sometimes (coldstart).

Alex C: So KEDA poll interval 30s + HPA relies on CPU. If queue spikes, KEDA activation might take one poll cycle before starting scale, then pod init adds 20s, and readinessProbe plus kube scheduling adds more => 504s.

Sarah L: Repro steps we did: 1) Send synthetic burst of 200 concurrent /v1/generate requests to model-pool-a, 2) observe queue length exceed 50, 3) KEDA emits ScaleEvent 30s later, 4) new pod scheduled, 5) pod takes ~22s to become Ready, 6) requests during warmup get 504.

Mike R: We also saw HPA behaving weirdly: CPU utilization barely ticks until pod is warm because model worker threads only spike after warm start. So HPA doesn't scale proactively.

Julia P: Proposed mitigations: 
- Lower KEDA pollingInterval to 5-10s and reduce cooldownPeriod to 60s for this pool.
- Add a lightweight startup prewarm endpoint that returns quickly and triggers worker init earlier.
- Increase minReplicas to 4 for this pool to reduce coldstarts during predictable hours.
- Adjust readinessProbe to check a fast health endpoint rather than full model init.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident task created: INC-7893 assigned to @eng-runtime and @oncall.

Alex C: Quick config to try (tested in staging): 
```yaml
scaledObject.spec.pollingInterval: 10
scaledObject.spec.cooldownPeriod: 60
hpa.spec.minReplicas: 4
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/fast
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 3
  timeoutSeconds: 2
  periodSeconds: 5
```

Caroline S: Will open a customer-facing note: "We're throttling scale backoffs and prewarming to reduce 504s; investigating root cause and will follow up." Assigned to me to update CS-4321.

Sarah L: Additional diagnostics we captured: kube-scheduler logs show pod pending due to node resource fragmentation for ~6s; container logs show model download occasionally spikes ~5-10s when pulling quantized params. Suggest pinning images on warm pools or pre-pulling in node init.

Mike R: Also saw this in monitoring: prefix cache hit rate drops during bursts -> more model work per request -> higher init CPU once pod starts -> HPA eventually scales but too late.

Julia P: Actions agreed: 
1) Apply scaledObject pollingInterval=10 & cooldown=60 (rollout canary to 10% first).
2) Raise minReplicas to 4 in prod for model-pool-a during business hours.
3) Implement fast /health/fast readiness and change probe.
4) Add node pre-pull hook for heavy model images.
5) Follow-up runbook update documenting KEDA+HPA interaction and recommended defaults.

Caroline S: I'll update CS ticket and ask customer to confirm reduced errors after rollout. ETA for config deploy: 30m for canary, 2h for full rollout.

Alex C: One-off mitigation for now: create short-lived circuit-breaker rule to return 429 for requests that queue >60s to avoid cascading retries.

Sarah L: I'll own the rollout and monitor 1min/5min gateway 504 rate. Tagging @oncall for monitoring during the change window.

eng-oncall-bot: Change window scheduled: 2024-11-09T04:00:00Z -> 2024-11-09T06:00:00Z.

Caroline S: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Will post post-mortem and add checklist to incidents runbook once stable.
